mission: Attack the consent system beyond e21's happy-path lifecycle: concurrent grant/withdraw races, replayed consent decisions, version-downgrade attempts, training-eligibility leaks after withdrawal across every selection code path, ledger export tampering detection, SQL-level append-only bypass via the service layer.
verdict_rationale: 6 of 7 confirmed abuses are fixed with regression tests running against real PostgreSQL. The 7th (a superuser/table-owner DB role can disable the append-only triggers) is unfixable inside the service layer and is recorded as a proven negative requiring a role-separation change outside this workstream's ownership.

dataset_scope.holdout_cases_touched: none (wm-dink-01 and afn-vic-rally1 not read, listed, or referenced)
dataset_scope.fixtures: All consent fixtures are synthetic: DB rows created inside a throwaway PostgreSQL schema, and file fixtures whose subject pseudonyms are prefixed SYNTHETIC-TEST-FIXTURE. No dataset records were added or rewritten.
dataset_scope.evaluation_grouping: n/a — this is an adversarial correctness workstream, not a model evaluation. Every case is grouped by an independent synthetic consent subject (one app_user + one pseudonymous ledger per case); no per-frame or per-clip splits are involved.

new_env_vars: CONSENT_EXPORT_SIGNING_KEY (unset => unsigned v1 export, current behaviour preserved)

training_eligible_media_selection_paths: services/api/src/modules/privacy/routes.ts legacy ml_training_consent read/write (does not select media; ledger is authoritative)
services/media-worker/src/worker.ts deletion path (sets removed_at, never selects for training)
packages/first-party-intake/src/intake.ts + consentRef.ts (export-envelope gate at intake time)
packages/swing-lab/src/exportDataset.ts (per-capture consent.state gate, no ledger read)
attack_surface_enumerated.conclusion: All user-sourced training selection flows through trainingConsent.ts; no unguarded SELECT of ml_dataset_item for training use exists elsewhere in the repo (grep of ml_dataset_item / ml_training_consent across all *.ts and *.sql).

findings.title: Replayed consent decision resurrects consent after withdrawal
findings.observed: POST /v1/me/consent/grant carried no decision identity, so a captured or offline-queued grant re-delivered after a withdrawal appended a fresh 'granted' row and made the subject training-eligible again. Reproduced against real Fastify + PostgreSQL.
findings.fix: Optional single-use decisionId (partial unique index ux_consent_record_decision_id, INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING => 409 consent.decision_replayed) plus decidedAtIso staleness check: a decision stamped before the scope's seq-latest ledger action is rejected 409 consent.decision_stale.

findings.title: consent_subject pseudonym repointing re-attributes an append-only ledger
findings.observed: The service role could UPDATE consent_subject.pseudonym (or user_id), aiming one account at another subject's ledger — inheriting that subject's grants, i.e. a training-eligibility leak — while consent_record itself stayed untouched and 'append-only'.
findings.fix: 0017 BEFORE UPDATE trigger consent_subject_pseudonym_immutable makes both pseudonym and user_id immutable.

findings.title: Silent attribution erasure by deleting the mapping row
findings.observed: consent_record has no FK to consent_subject (by design), so DELETE FROM consent_subject orphaned the ledger: /status and /export reported an empty history while the rows survived, and the erasure left no trace.
findings.fix: 0017 tombstones every mapping deletion into append-only consent_subject_erasure (BEFORE DELETE trigger; erasure table itself rejects UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE). findOrphanedLedgerSubjects (services/api/src/modules/consent/integrity.ts) surfaces ledger subjects orphaned WITHOUT a tombstone.

findings.title: Arbitrary and downgraded consent versions accepted
findings.observed: consentVersion was any 1..64-char string: 'totally-made-up-v9' was accepted and recorded as the authorizing contract, and a re-grant under model-training-v1 while model-training-v2 was on record silently downgraded the authorizing contract (including through a withdraw/regrant cycle).
findings.fix: checkConsentVersionAcceptable in packages/shared-types/src/consent.ts (scope-canonical <prefix>-v<major>, numeric major comparison, upgrades allowed, downgrades rejected) wired into the grant route => 400 consent.version_rejected. Contract shape versioned, not softened.

findings.title: Export tampering and stale-export replay were undetectable
findings.observed: The v1 export envelope's integrity fields (recordCount, maxSeq, recordsSha256) are all recomputable by whoever holds the file: dropping the trailing withdrawal and rehashing produced an envelope that passed every check and authorized intake (demonstrated in F23-5a). A genuine older export taken before a withdrawal also authorized intake indefinitely.
findings.fix: Export contract v2 (consent-ledger-export-v2): HMAC-SHA256 signature over the canonical envelope header, emitted when CONSENT_EXPORT_SIGNING_KEY is set. Intake verifies it via loadConsentLedger(path, { signingKey, minMaxSeq }); a configured host refuses unsigned v1 envelopes and bare arrays (no signature downgrade), and rejects an envelope whose maxSeq is behind the subject's already-seen watermark (stale replay). v1 is left intact and unsoftened for keyless consumers.

findings.title: Capture-mode narrowing was unenforced — a narrowed grant authorized every clip
findings.observed: consent_record.capture_mode was recorded on grants but read by no selector. A grant scoped to 'imported_video' therefore authorized the user's automatic-trigger captures too: a training-eligibility leak wider than the consent given.
findings.fix: trainingConsent.ts now requires the authorizing grant to be capture_mode = 'all_captures' in selectTrainingEligibleItems and verifyTrainingEligibility. ml_dataset_item carries no capture-mode provenance, so narrowed (or mode-less) grants authorize nothing — fail closed rather than over-select.

findings.title: PROVEN NEGATIVE: append-only is only as strong as the DB role
findings.observed: Through the service connection every mutation is blocked: UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE on consent_record all raise 'consent_record is append-only' (verified). But the test/dev connection owns the tables, and an owner/superuser role can ALTER TABLE consent_record DISABLE TRIGGER ALL and then rewrite or delete history — reproduced during probing. No service-layer code change can prevent this.
findings.fix: Not fixable within this ownership boundary. Requires role separation: the application connects as a non-owner role holding INSERT/SELECT only, with table ownership and trigger rights held by a migration role, plus an out-of-band ledger digest witness. Left as an honest negative rather than a weakened claim; migrations 0015/0016 remain unmodified.

non_findings: Concurrent grant/withdraw: 12 interleaved requests (6 grants + 6 withdrawals) all returned 200, produced exactly 12 append-only rows in monotonically increasing seq order, and derived status matched the seq-latest row and the training gate exactly. Per-subject pg_advisory_xact_lock was added so the version and staleness checks resolve against committed state rather than a stale read.
Withdrawal always flags dataset items (removed_at) and a re-grant never un-removes them (existing RT-3 still passes).
Legacy privacy-center revoke still reaches the ledger (RT-1 unchanged); the legacy ml_training_consent table is not consulted by any training selector.
SQL-like payloads in consentVersion/device/strokeIntent are inert: every query is parameterized (probed with quote/comment/DROP payloads; now additionally rejected by the version contract).
Default-deny holds: no records, mapping row without records, and orphaned ledgers all deny.

code: packages/shared-types/src/consent.ts (version contract helpers, export contract v2 + canonical signing payload)
services/api/src/modules/consent/routes.ts (version gate, replay/staleness gate, advisory lock, signed export)

honesty_notes: No Mac/iPhone/Apple Vision measurements, coach reviews, or Mobbin research are claimed — none were performed.
F23-5a is deliberately kept as a passing test that DEMONSTRATES the v1 forgery succeeding; the fix is the v2 contract, not a claim that v1 is safe.
F23-7 is reported as an unresolved architectural weakness rather than closed.
